title: The starter is the bakery
thesis: The slow invisible part of the work decides the result, long before anyone sees it.

nodes.text: There is a bakery where new bakers are not allowed to shape a loaf for their first month. They feed the starter.

evidence.filled_by: transcript line 3: first month, feed the starter, clean baskets, log temperature

nodes.text: The slow invisible part of the work decides the result, long before anyone sees it, and team leads who reward visible output are rewarding the wrong end.

evidence.filled_by: transcript line 11: 'patience with the slow invisible part of the work'

nodes.text: The failure happens before anyone looks: a weak starter cannot be rescued at the oven.

evidence.filled_by: transcript line 5: flat and sour, 'nobody can fix that at the oven', failure twelve hours earlier

nodes.text: A record of the slow part is how you find what went wrong instead of guessing.

evidence.filled_by: transcript line 7: eleven years of batch notebooks; reading back to the day the starter got tired

nodes.text: The person worth trusting is the one who notices the slow part, not the one with the best finish.

evidence.filled_by: transcript line 9: rainy-day rise, adjusting water temperature, 'the moment she knew he would be good'

nodes.text: Objection: a month of groundwork is hazing that drives good people away. Answer: the baker who believed exactly that is the one who noticed the starter.

evidence.filled_by: transcript line 9: 'He thought it was hazing'

nodes.text: What a team lead should protect: their team's starter.
The brief has no team-side example of protected groundwork. The conclusion needs one, or it ends on the analogy alone.
